BB_WORKSPACE.description: Bitbucket Cloud workspace slug (the first path segment after https://bitbucket.org/, e.g. mycompany).

BB_REPO.description: Bitbucket Cloud repository slug (the second path segment after https://bitbucket.org/{workspace}/, e.g. payments-api).

BB_COMMIT.description: Full 40-char Git commit SHA whose Code Insights security reports should be imported (Bitbucket Code Insights reports are attached per-commit, typically the HEAD commit of a feature branch or the merge commit of a pull request).

BB_MIN_SEVERITY.description: Optional minimum severity floor (info | low | medium | high | critical). Filters out lower-severity annotations client-side after Faraday severity normalisation. Defaults to info (no filtering).

BB_INCLUDE_NON_VULN.description: Optional flag (1 | true | yes) — when set, also import non-vulnerability annotations (CODE_SMELL / BUG / TEST). Defaults to false (only SECURITY-type reports and VULNERABILITY-type annotations import).

name: bitbucket_security
title: Bitbucket Cloud Code Insights
description: Bitbucket Cloud Code Insights REST API importer. Pulls Code Insights security reports (and their annotations) from a Bitbucket Cloud repository at a specific commit and emits Faraday bulk-create JSON to stdout. Lists Code Insights reports posted against the commit via /2.0/repositories/{workspace}/{repo}/commit/{commit}/reports (paginated via page / pagelen), filters to SECURITY-type reports (set BB_INCLUDE_NON_VULN=1 to also import CODE_SMELL / BUG / TEST), then pulls per-report annotations via /2.0/repositories/{workspace}/{repo}/commit/{commit}/reports/{report_id}/annotations. Each Bitbucket repository becomes one Faraday host (synthetic 0.0.0.0 ip because Code Insights findings live in source repos and pull-request diffs, not on IPs) with hostnames = {workspace}/{repo}; per-commit annotations attached as Faraday vulnerabilities — one per annotation with [SAST] engine prefix, path:line source location, annotation_type / report title / reporter / report_id / commit / result / created / updated timestamps and annotation_id surfacing in the description; resolution / remediation / recommendation / solution / fix surfaces as Faraday resolution. Refs include CWE-* (single + list + list-of-dict shapes with the CWE- prefix collapsed), OWASP categories (single + list), BitbucketRule-<rule>, BitbucketCheck-<check>, plus any URLs from links / references and the annotation's top-level link field. CVE list harvested from cve / cveId / cveName / cves (string + list-of-string + list-of-dict shapes, deduped case-insensitively). Severity normalised from Bitbucket Code Insights's string enum (CRITICAL / HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW — also accepts Minor / Moderate / Informational / Information / None / Unknown) with CVSS v3 bucketing as a fallback when only a numeric score is given (≤0 info, <4 low, <7 medium, <9 high, ≥9 critical); client-side BB_MIN_SEVERITY floor enforced after normalisation. Status mapped from the annotation's result field (FAILED / SKIPPED / PENDING → open, PASSED → closed, IGNORED → risk-accepted) with boolean triage flags (false_positive / ignored / suppressed / fixed / resolved) as fallbacks. Auth: HTTP Basic with BB_USER + BB_APP_PASSWORD; BB_APP_PASSWORD is a Bitbucket Cloud App Password (Personal Settings → App passwords) with repository:read scope at minimum — the legacy username:password combination is rejected by Bitbucket Cloud since 2022, so an App Password or Workspace Access Token is required. A pre-built 'Bearer <token>' value in BB_APP_PASSWORD (Workspace / Project / Repository Access Token) is also accepted and routed to the Authorization header verbatim. BB_HOST defaults to https://api.bitbucket.org for Bitbucket Cloud; set it to your Bitbucket Data Center API host (e.g. https://bitbucket.corp.example.com) for self-hosted deployments.
